**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The WARRANTY rule is satisfied here, on a somewhat unusual fact pattern:

- **Direction check.** This is a co-development agreement in which PB (our client) is the performing/development party and SFJ is principally the funder — SFJ is not a services/software vendor. So the rule's focus properly falls on whether the disclaimer strips warranties we rely on, and whether SFJ stands behind what it does undertake.
- **Express warranties exist and are largely mutual.** Article 13 covers authority (13.1.1), no conflicting agreements (13.1.2), compliance with law (13.1.3 Anti-Corruption Laws, 13.1.4 debarment, 13.1.5 permits/certifications), plus SFJ's funding-capacity warranty (13.5).
- **Performance standard.** Section 2.2.2 binds SFJ to conduct trials and perform assigned responsibilities in compliance with the Protocol, Applicable Laws and the Agreement, and "Applicable Laws" expressly includes GCP/GLP/GMP and ICH guidelines — the industry-standard analogue of "professional and workmanlike."
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranties.** 13.6.2 is prefaced "EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13," so this is not walk-away "AS IS" territory.
- **Noted, not flagged.** There is no conformance period or repair/replace/refund mechanic, but there are no software deliverables for it to attach to; remedies run through Article 12 indemnification and Article 14 termination. The 13.6.1 outcome disclaimer is mutual and, since PB generates the Research Results, works in our favour — so we leave it alone. PB's heavier warranty package is the negotiated funding bargain and belongs to the reps/diligence rules, not this one.
